reason: Start with the kidney filter to follow what happens to the blood sample.
expectation: I expect fluid and small dissolved substances to enter the nephron, while blood cells remain in the vessels.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter also retains most proteins; next I want to follow recovery from the tubule.
reaction: The distinction between small solutes and most proteins makes the filter's selectivity clear.
reason: Add the transporters to see which useful substances return to the blood.
expectation: I expect selective transporters to recover some dissolved substances from the tubule into nearby blood, though the result may specify which ones.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the drainage route, but recovery comes first in the stated goal.

effect: The tubule recovers glucose and other useful substances; I can now follow water recovery.
reaction: The note that healthy kidneys normally recover almost all filtered glucose makes the recovery step more concrete.
reason: Add the water-permeable tubule to continue following the filtered fluid.
expectation: I expect some water to move from the tubule back toward the blood, leaving a more concentrated fluid.

alternatives.reason: The ureters are part of the drainage route, but I want to finish following recovery first.

effect: Water returns to the blood while wastes remain in the tubule; I can now follow the remaining fluid into drainage.
reaction: The picture makes the contrast between water recovery and retained waste clear.
reason: Use urinary drainage to continue the sample's route toward urine.
expectation: I expect the remaining fluid to pass into the urinary drainage route as urine.

alternatives.reason: Fitting the ureters would build the organ route, but I want to finish following the sample first.

effect: The sample reaches the bladder as urine, completing the filtration and recovery goal; the urinary organs still need connecting.
reaction: The ureter-to-bladder picture closes the sample's route, though it is a predictable step.
reason: Fit the ureters to begin assembling the urinary organs.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to connect.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs fitting, but the ureters connect directly to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are fitted; the bladder remains to be connected.
reaction: The fitting is straightforward, with little new detail.
reason: Fit the bladder to complete the visible urinary drainage assembly; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the bladder to connect to the ureters, leaving the assembled organs ready to join the body.

effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder are assembled; they can now be connected to the body.
reaction: The explanation makes the drainage route clear, though the fitting was predictable.
reason: Connect the urinary organs to the body; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the kidneys and urinary drainage organs to join the body and complete the remaining goal.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to circulation, completing the urinary-system goal and the chapter.
reaction: The final picture ties filtration back to the body, though the connection was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following selective recovery was most worthwhile: the planned picture and explanation show glucose returning to blood and explain that healthy kidneys normally recover almost all filtered glucose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters added little detail beyond the already shown urine route, so it felt repetitive.

surprise.text: The distinction that most proteins, as well as blood cells, remain in the blood made the filter's selectivity clearer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although fitting the organs after seeing urine reach the bladder repeated a route already established.

continue.text: I would probably continue: following filtration and recovery into an organ-level connection was useful, even if the final fittings were predictable. That is my judgment of the supplied text and illustration plans, not evidence of student comprehension or enjoyment.
